verdict: Spaghetti bolognese is lower in calories. But chicken chop can be a good choice if you change the sides.
why: Spaghetti is an estimated 600 kcal, a chicken chop set an estimated 850 kcal. About a 250 kcal difference.
Spaghetti fat is 22 g, chicken chop 43 g, almost double.
Chicken chop wins on protein: 40 g vs 25 g. That's its advantage.
A lot of the extra calories in chicken chop come from the fries and sauce. That part you can control.
when_a: Chicken chop is okay when you ask to swap the fries for salad or vegetables, and ask for the sauce on the side.
when_b: Spaghetti is okay when you want a lighter western meal. Add a side salad or vegetable soup so you're fuller.
tip: At western food stalls, ask for sauce on the side and dip a little at a time. Even better, choose grilled chicken chop, not fried.

faq.q: Is there a big difference between grilled and fried chicken chop?
faq.a: Usually grilled is lower in fat because there's no batter or frying oil. The estimated difference can be quite big, depending on the shop.

faq.q: Spaghetti is carbs, won't it make me fat?
faq.a: Carbs aren't the enemy. What matters is your total daily calories. A plate of spaghetti can fit, just don't add garlic bread and a sweet drink at the same time.
